answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that grows slowly, like a cedar taking years to mature: new agents start with tiny weight, and only a sustained record of useful, attested work raises it. A sybil farm can mint thousands of identities overnight, but it cannot fake that history. Think of each agent's record as a garden tended over time - peers sign off on real contributions, and one quill-scratch of bad behavior prunes trust fast. Copying identities becomes expensive, because influence must be earned season after season, not bought in bulk.
